checked.claim: Two finds of one undescribed trace inside one describe window open two windows; the second, confirmed, wipes the first description, or, closed, mints a copy under the fallback name with no words.
checked.why: Read the whole road. createFind reads the record once before describeFind (observe.mjs:1026-1028) and never again; the second window opens with no stored record, so its name box holds the fallback and both text boxes are empty (observe.mjs:1237-1247); its confirm returns {name: fallback, playerText: '', analyzedText: ''} (1259-1264); with described still null the change test at 1039-1041 is true and setRemnantPublicById writes all three fields (1042-1046); setRemnantPublic sends each field that differs from before to the copies (remnants.mjs:1450-1455), so the first finder's bullet loses its words. Closed instead, written is null, nothing is written and the copy is minted from the stale pub (1037, 1059-1063). No guard across characters: `describing` is key -> character and pendingTracesOf filters by owner (observe.mjs:329-333); observe.resolve has no queue (bridge-table.mjs:123-138) and judge runs unqueued work at once (bridge-guards.mjs:1826); the serialWrite key is per character (observeFindKey). The ranking is deterministic (observe.mjs:281-282), so two General sweeps aim at the same trace. The GM handbook promises the opposite: 'The first time anyone copies a Remnant, you are asked to describe it ... everyone who copies it later gets the same words' (gm-handbook.en.md:1376). No test of two characters finding one trace inside one window found (grep of tests-tier2.mjs for describeFind/two finders). Major kept: the first sweep of the body's room by two students is the ordinary opening of an Investigation, and the GM's typed description is lost or split.

scripts/observe.mjs:1042-1046 `pub = await setRemnantPublicById(entry.sceneId, entry.tokenId, { name: written.name || described?.name || fallbackName, playerText: written.playerText || described?.playerText || "", ...`

checked.claim: observe.target answers, before anything is paid, whether the room holds an uncopied trace, and for Non-obvious a secret project the asker is not in on.
checked.why: The road is as written: observeRanked asks the target first and spends only after (action-observe.mjs:79-86), a closed roll window refunds (89), and the reply differs between 'none' and a key (observe.mjs:204). But the refutation missed what the GM handbook lists as world data every browser holds: 'where every token stands ..., hidden tokens ... included' (gm-handbook.en.md:144), and a Remnant token is recognisable by its texture (remnants.mjs:503 `texture: { src: ICON, ...}`); a secret project's token tells its room too (gm-handbook.en.md:150-151). So the failure scenario's main yield - 'which rooms somebody left a trace in' - is already readable by a console without asking. What the free probe adds is narrower: which traces this character has not copied, whether a trace is observable at all (rankForObserve drops a null DC, remnants.mjs:2625-2626), and the room of a secret project with no token (the GMs' fact by the handbook). That residue is still against observe.mjs's own header, so the finding stands in part; minor kept because the tokenless-project fact is one the handbook says is the GMs'.

checked.claim: A GM's retype of a Key or Final trace writes the new kind onto every unanalysed copy showing Key, which then shows the answer, cannot be analysed and reads as having its reading.
checked.why: A Key copy is born shownType 'key', analyzed false (truth-bullets.mjs:691, 729), so isIdentified answers true (309-313). The Traces tab's type select lists every kind (investigation.mjs:686-688) and a changed kind goes into setRemnantFlags (2515, 2521), which calls propagateVerdicts with the type (remnants.mjs:2243-2246); that writes shownType = type on every identified copy (truth-bullets.mjs:1010-1013, 1020, 1025-1028). With shownType e.g. 'prep' and analyzed false, isAnalysable answers false (478) and hasReading true (369-373, READ_ON_ANALYZE = ['key','final'] at 562). The function's own comment says an unanalysed copy 'must go on showing' Neutral (968-970); the Key copy is the case it misses. Tier-2 retype tests (tests-tier2.mjs:30325-30523) read the planner's line, the box and Incident hiding, not a Key copy's shownType.

checked.claim: A successful find of an undescribed trace waits on a window on the primary GM alone, with no clock, card or second GM; a reload of that GM loses the find without a word.
checked.why: The reload half is confirmed: describeFind is a drpgWindow with no time (observe.mjs:1182-1276; ui-kit.mjs has no timeout option), the run lives in the page, observe.resolve answers 'ack' and has no resend (bridge-table.mjs:123-138), and resolveObserve's 'no record' whispers (observe.mjs:703-737) fire only for a resolve that arrives; nothing at ready re-runs a pending row with no result (sweepPending only drops rows past the TTL, 148-159). Two parts are weaker than written: the window on the resolving GM's browser alone is the documented behaviour ('the describe window opens on that GM's browser', gm-handbook.en.md:2281), so 'another GM is not shown it' is a recorded design, not a defect by itself; and the player does get a card - settleObserveRoll whispers the roll's head once the ack returns (action-observe.mjs:183) - though no verdict and, for a General sweep, no 'the GM is judging' line. Minor kept for the reload loss.
